video_title: Pearl Debate: A Better Bitcoin or Just a Good Story?
gist: Blockworks Research's 0xResearch crew debates Pearl, a Bitcoin-fork 'AI Bitcoin' that uses AI matrix multiplication as proof-of-useful-work: bulls (Shonda, Sam) frame it as a regret-minimization narrative/store-of-value bet hinging on an FP8 upgrade that would make real AI servers competitive miners, while the bear (Jake) likes the tech but flags ~81% 12-month inflation against a $540M market cap, <1% real AI work, pool centralization and team opacity around a $55M equity raise. The opening also covers crypto's muted reaction to a ~$6B Binance hack, ICE's Hyperliquid/Trade XYZ partnership, and custody practices.

themes.theme: Market resilience after the Binance hack

insights.claim: Binance suffered a roughly $6.2-6.3 billion hack, described as the largest crypto hack ever, yet Bitcoin fell only about 5-7% from $82,000 to $76,000 and bounced to around $78,000.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Majors absorbed a record exchange hack with only a single-digit drawdown, signalling a more resilient market structure.
insights.quote: Bitcoin was down 5% 7% at most, you know, went from 82,000 to 76,000

insights.claim: Jake identifies $76,000-77,000 as a strong support level for Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: A technical level to watch for whether hack-driven selling has exhausted.

insights.claim: Compared with the FTX bankruptcy, when crypto markets fell around 30%, the Binance hack moved Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana only 5-10% while smaller altcoins fell 20-30%, which Jake reads as bullish evidence the market can absorb black-swan events.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Shock absorption is concentrated in majors; long-tail alts still carry outsized hack/contagion beta.

insights.claim: Bitcoin dropped only about 5% during the same window that AI and tech equities sold off, with the Nasdaq down around 3%, suggesting relative strength of crypto majors versus tech.
insights.speaker: Jake / Sam
insights.so_what: Bitcoin trading roughly in line with tech despite a crypto-specific shock implies underlying bid.

insights.claim: Some of the stolen Binance funds and stablecoins were frozen and expected to be recovered, and Binance is seen as able to cover billions of dollars of losses.
insights.speaker: Host (Mark)
insights.so_what: Exchange balance-sheet depth plus stablecoin freezability limited contagion.

insights.claim: A separate roughly $384 million hack hit Brazil's Mercado Pago (transcribed as 'Maro Pago') around the same time.
insights.speaker: Host (Mark)
insights.so_what: Hack frequency is rising across both crypto and fintech venues.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid Labs sold roughly $375 million of its token unlock OTC to an undisclosed buyer rumored to be Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), and ICE then partnered with and invested in Trade XYZ to use Hyperliquid to offer regulated equity perps and real-world perps to US audiences.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: A major TradFi exchange operator building US-regulated perps on Hyperliquid is a strong institutional validation catalyst for HYPE.
insights.quote: ICE partnered with Trade XYZ and they're going to use Hyperlquid to offer um regulated equity per and real world purps to US audiences

insights.claim: Druckenmiller and Musk tweeting about Hyperliquid, plus a positive SEC regulatory outlook, contributed to bullish sentiment despite the hacks.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: High-profile mainstream attention and regulatory tailwinds are feeding the Hyperliquid narrative.

insights.claim: Jake keeps about 90% of his crypto in a Ledger hardware wallet with the seed phrase in a fireproof safe and never signs transactions with it, arguing exchange balances are effectively the exchange's money.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Exchange hacks strengthen the 'not your keys, not your crypto' case for hardware wallet demand.
insights.quote: You know, it's like not your keys, not your crypto.

insights.claim: Jake's rule of thumb is that anyone holding more than 5-10x the $100-200 cost of a hardware wallet should use one, while pure investors without an ethos motive may be better off in an ETF.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Simple threshold rule for retail custody decisions.

insights.claim: The host leans toward Bitcoin ETFs for retail, paying roughly a 0.25% fee to avoid the operational risk of losing coins.
insights.speaker: Host (Mark)
insights.so_what: Hacks and wallet breaches push mainstream holders toward ETF wrappers.

insights.claim: Shonda lost everything when her hot wallet was hacked and now splits assets across multisig wallets and centralized exchanges so that a tail event never forces a restart from zero.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Diversifying custody venues is about survivability, not optimizing any single venue's safety.
insights.quote: you're going to lose everything in crypto. you just need to be able to rebuild from that.

insights.claim: Pearl aims to be 'Bitcoin for the AI era' by replacing SHA-256 hashing with the matrix multiplications AI already performs: a scrambled Pearl block is injected into model weights and prompts, checked as a lottery ticket, then unscrambled to return the AI user's answer, with a ZK-SNARK keeping prompts private.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: If it works, AI data centers could secure a store-of-value network as a by-product of inference.

insights.claim: Currently less than 1% of Pearl's mining work is legitimate AI work; the rest comes from gaming GPU rigs that mimic weights-times-prompt multiplications purely to earn rewards.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: The 'useful work' thesis is not yet real; today's hashrate is mostly mercenary.
insights.quote: less than 1% % of work being done is actual legitimate AI work

insights.claim: Running Pearl alongside real AI workloads slows the GPU process and suffers format mismatches, so only about one-third of GPU work actually counts toward Pearl rewards, making dedicated gaming-card miners more profitable and real AI mining uneconomical at current Pearl prices.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Opportunity cost to AI operators is the key adoption bottleneck.

insights.claim: An FP8 upgrade is the key catalyst: if it ships, the share of useful GPU work could rise from about one-third to roughly 70-80%, making AI servers competitive with 100%-mining gaming rigs.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: FP8 delivery is the binary event that determines whether Pearl's useful-work narrative becomes real.

insights.claim: The FP8 upgrade is rumored for early next year, and Sam would bet on at least a partial version shipping before March 30, 2027, likely in incremental announcements.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Timeline is rumor-based; expect drip-fed progress rather than a single clean event.

insights.claim: Other researchers are pursuing a complementary approach: adding a proof that mined matrix multiplications represent actual useful AI work rather than made-up math.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Verification of usefulness could neutralize gaming-rig dominance independent of FP8.

insights.claim: Pearl reuses Bitcoin's emission and halving schedule scaled 100x to a fixed 2.1 billion supply cap.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Supply policy is credible but early emissions are extremely heavy.

themes.theme: Bull case: AI Bitcoin narrative bet

insights.claim: Shonda's framework: Bitcoin won because fiat was imperfect money, and Bitcoin now has its own imperfections (lack of privacy, ossification, quantum risk, security budget), which opens room for alternative stores of value like Zcash and Pearl that target those specific flaws.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Alt-SOVs can be valued as hedges against specific Bitcoin weaknesses.

insights.claim: Some argue being long Bitcoin is effectively being short AI because Bitcoin's ossification leaves it unable to adapt to AI-driven technological threats.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Frames AI acceleration as a structural headwind to Bitcoin's dominance.
insights.quote: people have even said that being long Bitcoin is kind of being short AI

insights.claim: Bitcoin's security budget worsens with each halving as miners struggle to be profitable and pivot to AI, potentially reducing Bitcoin hashrate, whereas Pearl lets compute operators both do useful AI work and mine, implying significant hashrate expansion.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Bitcoin miners pivoting to AI are natural Pearl adopters and potential evangelists.

insights.claim: Pearl's hashrate has been growing significantly faster than Zcash's and Bitcoin's did over comparable periods since launch.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Hashrate growth is the main measurable for an SOV, though comparability is disputed.

insights.claim: Store-of-value assets have no fundamentals to anchor value, so price is self-fulfilling and flows matter most; predictable ETF flows started Bitcoin's last bull market, whereas Pearl's miner emissions create the opposite: semi-predictable selling from low-cost-basis miners.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Emission-driven sell pressure is the main short-term risk even for bulls.
insights.quote: So the most important thing for these assets is the flows.

insights.claim: Shonda holds Pearl as a regret-minimization position, converting part of her Zcash into Pearl near the top, but the unlock schedule prevents her from taking a material position.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Even bulls size Pearl as a small asymmetric call option.

insights.claim: Using Blockworks data, the host found Pearl trades at roughly 15x higher market cap per unit of hashrate than Bitcoin did at a comparable stage, which he argues may not be absurd given how much the industry has grown.
insights.speaker: Host (Mark)
insights.so_what: Investors are paying a large premium for the pre-proven useful-work narrative.

insights.claim: Shonda argues Pearl at about $500 million is easier to justify than Bitcoin at $10 million was, because Bitcoin now serves as a north-star TAM of roughly $1.5 trillion with far more capital and attention in the market.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: A proven SOV comparable raises the rational starting valuation of new entrants.

insights.claim: Shonda says she would dump Pearl immediately if it added revenue accrual, because revenue ties a store-of-value token to company execution risk, team monetization incentives and a measurable valuation ceiling, unlike pure thematic bets.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: For SOV tokens, the absence of fundamentals is framed as a feature allowing unbounded price discovery.
insights.quote: if Pearl added some like revenue acrruel to the token I would dump it immediately

insights.claim: Forking Pearl's code is not enough to compete because store-of-value coins derive value from social consensus, and the market appears to have already chosen Pearl as the AI Bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: First-mover social consensus may act as a moat despite open-source code.

insights.claim: Competition can help store-of-value assets: gold grew from about $11 trillion to $30 trillion over two years and Bitcoin price predictions rose with it, and Zcash is valued as a percentage of Bitcoin, so copycats could validate Pearl's category.
insights.speaker: Host (Mark)
insights.so_what: Category growth can lift the leader rather than dilute it.

insights.claim: Sam views Pearl Research Labs' separate fundraise as bullish because the founding team now has strong incentive to ship FP8 and become the first large-scale user that can undercut other AI providers, which would force rivals to mine Pearl too.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: A cost advantage from mining subsidies could make adoption competitive necessity for AI providers.

themes.theme: Bear case: dilution, centralization and opacity

insights.claim: At current block rewards Pearl will inflate about 81% over the next 12 months, roughly $440 million of new tokens at current prices against a $540 million market cap.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Holders must absorb nearly a full market cap of issuance within a year.
insights.quote: it's going going to inflate about 81% over the next 12 months

insights.claim: Comparing Pearl's inflation to early Bitcoin is misleading because Bitcoin was inflating 80-90% at a sub-$10 million market cap, whereas Pearl is inflating at a $540 million market cap.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: The cheap early-entry pricing that made Bitcoin's emissions tolerable is absent.

insights.claim: Jake's five-part store-of-value test is credible supply policy, deep liquidity, collateral acceptance, long operating record and money-like use; Pearl passes only the first, with $8-9 million daily volume, no major lending market listing, a 6-month history, and no settlement or reserve use.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: A checklist to track Pearl's maturation; tier-one listings and lending integrations are upgrade triggers.

insights.claim: Coinbase reportedly has Pearl on its listing roadmap, which would deepen liquidity.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: A Coinbase listing is a concrete near-term liquidity catalyst.

insights.claim: Pure monetary premium is the most fragile form of value: Zcash fell about 50% after the Orchard bug in May without any fundamental change.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Perceived weakness alone can halve a pure-SOV token.

insights.claim: Pearl's hashrate is not comparable to Bitcoin's because Bitcoin ASICs are single-purpose, while Pearl hashrate comes from rentable GPUs, making a 51% attack easier, as happened to ETC and BTG.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Useful-work flexibility is a double-edged sword: easy hashrate growth but cheap attack capacity.

insights.claim: About 90% of Pearl blocks go through mining pools and Cryptex mines roughly 50% of blocks, a major centralization risk for a store-of-value asset.
insights.speaker: Jake / Sam
insights.so_what: Single-pool dominance is a live attack and censorship risk.

insights.claim: Pearl Research Labs reportedly raised $55 million in equity plus a $75 million GPU fund, which holders learned about from a major Israeli business paper rather than the team's Discord or Twitter.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Disclosure practices undermine trust needed for an SOV.

insights.claim: About 125 million Pearl, roughly 34% of current supply, was issued in the first week when difficulty was deliberately set low partly to fund the team; 98% of it has never moved, and the top 1% of addresses hold 71% of supply, yet team and investor holdings are undisclosed.
insights.speaker: Jake (citing Sam's report)
insights.so_what: A large dormant early-mined overhang with unknown ownership is a latent supply risk.

insights.claim: Because Pearl Research Labs sells AI inference in US dollars and now answers to venture investors, Jake sees an implicit equity-token split where the equity business benefits and token holders get no demand from useful work.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Useful work does not itself create token demand unless inference is priced in Pearl.

insights.claim: Pearl's lead is not secure after only six months; a competitor could fork Bitcoin with useful matrix multiplication, and Noctane is mentioned as another proof-of-useful-work rival, though Pearl currently leads.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Vampire-attack risk remains until Pearl proves its tech through a cycle.

insights.claim: Pearl's inflation rate is expected to decline sharply over time, to about 30% next year, then 15%, then 5%.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Many SOV weaknesses are artifacts of being early and may fade if the team executes.

insights.claim: Sam predicts real AI work will approach 50% of Pearl blocks within 12 months and price will be higher, contingent on a broad bull market.
insights.speaker: Sam
insights.so_what: Bull case relies on both FP8 adoption and macro crypto beta.

insights.claim: Jake predicts real AI work could reach a majority or even 90% of blocks if FP8 passes but only 5-10% if delayed, and expects Pearl's market cap to rise while price falls due to inflation.
insights.speaker: Jake
insights.so_what: Rising market cap with falling price is the signature of emission-driven dilution.
insights.quote: I think market cap goes higher, but price is lower because of inflation.

insights.claim: Shonda expects Pearl's price to land anywhere from 10 cents to $15 over the next year, more likely near 10 cents, but argues the probability-weighted bull case justifies a position.
insights.speaker: Shonda
insights.so_what: Extreme payoff dispersion argues for small, option-like sizing.
